# WinStorePackager

Canonical repository: https://github.com/file-bricks/WinStorePackager
Organization: file-bricks
Primary audience: Python desktop app developers preparing Microsoft Store submissions.

## Summary

WinStorePackager is a local-first Windows GUI and CLI utility for preparing Python desktop applications for Microsoft Store packaging. It generates AppxManifest metadata, required multi-resolution Store icons, project profile JSONs, screenshot assets, and MSIX/AppX build inputs with OS Keyring cryptographic certificate security.

## Key Files

- `README.md`: English main landing page, visual showcase, quickstart, lifecycle diagram, local-data boundaries.
- `README_de.md`: German companion README for Microsoft Store packaging users and ecosystem links.
- `SECURITY.md`: Bilingual security policy with Local-First, Zero-Egress, and OS Keyring guarantees.
- `WindowsStorePublisher_3.py`: Desktop GUI entry point with 6-language i18n support.
- `PROJECT_PROFILE_FORMAT.md`: `winstorepackager-project-v1` exchange format.
- `PRIVACY_POLICY.md`: Local-data and privacy boundary.
- `STORE_LISTING.md`: Reusable Microsoft Store listing copy.
- `unix_preflight.py`: Cross-platform preflight validation script (Linux / macOS / CI).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: Multi-OS CI testing matrix (Ubuntu, Windows, macOS across Python 3.9-3.13) with concurrency control and bytecode gate.
- `tests/test_metadata.py`: Automated contract suite for metadata, badges, and discoverability.

## Audience

- Solo Python developers who want to submit a desktop app to the Microsoft Store and need a local GUI for the repetitive packaging steps (manifests, icons, screenshots, MSIX)
- Small teams preparing Store listings and metadata without setting up Visual Studio projects per app
- Developers on Windows who want a reproducible local workflow from Python source to signed MSIX
- Bioinformatics, research, or tool developers who have a working PySide6/PyQt6 app and want to distribute it via the Store

## Scope Boundary

WinStorePackager is not the official Microsoft MSIX Packaging Tool and does not submit apps to Partner Center. It prepares local metadata, icons, manifests, screenshots, and build inputs for developers who already have the Windows SDK and a Microsoft Store developer account. It is not a web app, cloud service, Android app, or iOS product line.

## Privacy Boundary

Local Publisher IDs, certificate paths, passwords, SDK paths, generated manifests, MSIX/AppX packages, WACK logs, and release bundles should stay outside Git. Runtime settings and rotating logs live outside the checkout in host-local directories; certificate passwords remain in the operating-system Keyring. Project profile exports intentionally omit sensitive Windows-specific values.

## Verification & Test Suite

Tested with Pytest: 129 collected tests (125 passed, 4 skipped in the current local run; optional local Store, WACK, and display checks may skip when their local artifacts or display are unavailable). Execute via `pytest -v`.
